title: He halted. I have passed the way to aunt Sara’s. Am I not going there? Seems not. No-one about. He turned northeast and crossed the firmer sand towards the
html_source:
In plot terms, Stephen is going to the National Library to deliver a letter for Deasy but mainly to deliver his theory on Hamlet to some literary figures. However Stephen doesn’t think about it at all in this chapter. Something else is going on. He has just left the Tower and said to himself that he won’t go back. He is at the time homeless. In this paragraph he indicates that he won’t go to his family (aunt Sara’s). The opportunity to go there leads to confused if not dark thoughts – maze of cunning nets, human shells, dreadful thirst, midden, man’s ashes.

In this paragraph he also shifts from this unsettling part of his life to ‘the firmer sand towards the Pigeon house’. This shift instigates thoughts/memories grounded in his experiences in Paris in which there are some home truths for Stephen but none of the dark words of the preceding paragraphs.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: I would also add that the dissociation between Stephen’s mind and feet “Am I not going there? Seems not” mirrors the alienation he felt of his lower body described earlier in this chapter.
